claims.claim: **KD is an acute vasculitis of medium vessels that favours the coronary arteries**; untreated, about 25% develop coronary artery aneurysms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complete KD = fever ≥4 days (day 1 = fever onset) AND at least 4 principal features at any point** (not necessarily together) **AND no better alternative explanation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Features appear sequentially — ask about ones that have already resolved.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Principal features:** bilateral non-exudative painless conjunctival injection, often limbal-sparing; polymorphous erythematous rash (not bullous, vesicular or haemorrhagic); palmar/plantar erythema with painful oedema and/or periungual desquamation at 2–3 weeks; unilateral tender anterior cervical nodes ≥1.5 cm; lip, tongue ('strawberry') or oropharyngeal erythema (not exudative or ulcerated).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incomplete KD:** suggestive presentation with fewer than 4 principal features; needs abnormal investigations to support it. **Infants and adolescents often present incompletely and have higher cardiac risk.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infants under 12 months with prolonged unexplained fever — even with normal inflammatory markers — should have an echocardiogram.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials:** a positive respiratory virus PCR does not exclude KD (about 1/3 are positive); consider KD when GAS infection fails to improve after 24–48 hours of antibiotics, and in an infant whose fever is prolonged, with aseptic meningitis or irritability that is unexplained.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High risk of CAA:** age ≤6 months, or right coronary or LAD Z-score ≥2.5.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other factors that may increase IVIg resistance or CAA risk:** age 6–12 months; coronary Z-score ≥2; IVIg ≥10 days after fever onset; IVIg resistance; KD shock syndrome or MAS; CRP ≥130 mg/L; Asian ethnicity (East, South or mixed); anaemia; hypoalbuminaemia; hyponatraemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No single test diagnoses KD.** Consider, for every child, FBE, CRP, ESR, UEC, LFTs, blood culture, urine microscopy and culture, ECG, and serum stored before IVIg. **Do not repeat ESR after IVIg** — it is falsely raised.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A normal echocardiogram does not exclude KD, and waiting for one should not delay treatment.** Suggested schedule: a baseline study when the child presents, then again at 4–6 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every child with KD gets IVIg 2 g/kg in one infusion**, usually with rates stepped up over 8–12 hours. Coronary outcomes are better with early treatment; timing per senior advice and local protocol.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give IVIg without delay when clinically safe; still give it beyond 10 days of fever if inflammation is active** (fever, raised markers, abnormal coronaries).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aspirin 5 mg/kg orally daily** to prevent thrombosis, continued until the cardiology follow-up review (~6 weeks after onset). Higher doses do not improve coronary outcomes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid NSAIDs while on aspirin** — ibuprofen may reduce its cardioprotective effect.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High CAA risk (or clinician discretion): add corticosteroids** — example regimen 2 mg/kg once daily IV methylprednisolone or oral prednisolone (max 50 mg), tapered over 2–4 weeks by response; follow local protocols or subspecialty advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IVIg resistance** (fever ≥38°C 36 hours or more after the first IVIg finishes): consider other causes and consult local KD experts; options include a **second IVIg dose** and adding **infliximab or corticosteroids**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antithrombotic therapy for CAAs is managed with cardiology.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resolving KD** (convalescent, no fever, normal markers): start aspirin and refer for echocardiography.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **KD shock syndrome** (hypotension, poor perfusion or myocardial dysfunction): consider a slower IVIg infusion. **Fever during infusion may be KD activity** — consider paracetamol 30 minutes before and regularly during.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delay live vaccines (MMR, MMRV, varicella, rotavirus) for 11 months after IVIg**; if measles exposure risk is high, vaccinate and repeat after 11 months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team whenever KD is suspected. Transfer** if the heart is involved or echocardiography cannot be done locally in good time.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Home once well and afebrile for ≥36 hours after treatment**, with daily aspirin, a follow-up plan including repeat echo, and education to re-present with fever or returning symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Kawasaki disease' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Kawasaki_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
